988.short: The national three-digit number for a mental health or suicide crisis. One of Alabama's four in-state call centers is at WellStone in Huntsville.

little-orange-fish.short: The Huntsville organization for which this report was prepared, and the publisher of the statewide companion report.

north-alabama-mental-health-coalition.short: A Huntsville-area coalition of mental health stakeholders, formed in 2015 by a committee of the Society of St. Vincent de Paul.

wellstone.short: The nonprofit community mental health center for Madison and Cullman counties. It also runs the Huntsville crisis center, a 988 call center and a pediatric crisis unit.

community-mental-health-center.short: One of the regional organizations that deliver public outpatient mental health care in Alabama. WellStone is the center for Madison and Cullman counties.

catchment.short: The set of counties a center is assigned to serve. It shows who is responsible for an area, not how far residents must travel or how much they use the center.

crisis-diversion-center.short: A place open at all hours where a person in a mental health crisis can walk in or be brought by police or ambulance, as an alternative to an emergency room or jail.

wellstone-emergency-services.short: WellStone's adult crisis center on Memorial Parkway in Huntsville. Its permanent building opened in September 2022, and the state assigns it fifteen counties.

pediatric-crisis-unit.term: Pediatric crisis unit (WellStone Pediatric Crisis Care)
pediatric-crisis-unit.short: WellStone's 24-bed crisis unit for young people in Huntsville, opened in late September 2024 and listed by the state with the adult crisis center.

probate-court.short: The county court that hears petitions for involuntary commitment in Alabama. Madison County's also runs an outpatient commitment program with WellStone.

admh.term: Alabama Department of Mental Health (the Department)
admh.short: The state agency for public mental health, substance use and developmental disability services. It certifies WellStone and names the counties each crisis center serves.

ccbhc.short: A clinic certified to provide a required set of mental health and substance use services to anyone who seeks care, and paid a daily rate by Medicaid. WellStone has been one since July 2024.

the-core.short: This report's name for Madison and Cullman counties, the two counties for which WellStone is the community mental health center.

the-ring.short: This report's name for the thirteen counties, beyond Madison and Cullman, that the state assigns to the Huntsville crisis center.

service-area.short: The public record draws WellStone's service area three ways: two counties for routine care, fifteen for the crisis center, and a Region 1 that has three meanings of its own.

region-1.short: A label with three different meanings in north Alabama: a mental illness services region, a 13-county Community Services office region and an 18-county police training region.

crisis-intervention-team.term: Crisis intervention training (Crisis Intervention Team, CIT)
crisis-intervention-team.short: Training that prepares police officers to respond to people in a mental health crisis. Huntsville Police is the training hub for an 18-county north Alabama region.

nami-alabama.short: The state organization of the National Alliance on Mental Illness and its local affiliate. Madison County has an affiliate; none is listed for Cullman County.

two-one-one.short: The telephone information and referral line for local help. Madison County's calls are answered in Huntsville and Cullman County's from Birmingham.

hud-continuum-of-care.short: A regional body, recognized by the federal housing department, that plans the local response to homelessness and runs the yearly count. Madison and Cullman are in different ones.

county-health-rankings.short: A national publication of county health measures. This report uses its rural share, provider ratios, and suicide and overdose death rates for the fifteen counties.

regional-310-board.short: A public corporation formed under Alabama's Act 310 of 1967 to contract with the Department of Mental Health. WellStone is the 310 board for mental illness in both counties.

national-childrens-advocacy-center.short: A Huntsville center, opened in 1985, that brings prosecutors, police, child welfare staff and therapists together on child abuse cases and offers trauma therapy to children.

north-alabama-regional-hospital.short: The state psychiatric hospital in Decatur, with 74 beds, whose closure the state announced in January 2015.

diversion.short: Steering a person away from jail or an emergency room and into care. It is the stated purpose of the crisis center, and no count of people diverted there has been published.

stepping-up.short: A national initiative to reduce the number of people with mental illness in county jails. Madison and Cullman counties were both first-year Alabama sites in 2018–19.

specialty-courts.term: Specialty courts (mental health, veterans and drug courts)
specialty-courts.short: Court dockets that put eligible defendants under supervised treatment in place of ordinary prosecution or jail. Both counties have set up mental health, veterans and drug court dockets.

assisted-outpatient-treatment.short: Court-ordered treatment in the community for a person who has been through the commitment process; in Madison County, run by the probate court with WellStone since 2020.

civil-commitment.short: A court order requiring a person with mental illness to accept treatment. In Alabama the county probate court hears the petition; it is not a criminal matter.

hb70-2022.term: House Bill 70 of 2022 (the revised commitment law)
hb70-2022.short: A 2022 Alabama law that added a ground for taking a person to a mental health facility and allowed courts to mandate outpatient care. It took effect in July 2022.

mobile-crisis.short: Clinicians who travel to a person in crisis, at home or elsewhere in the community. WellStone runs adult and child teams in both Madison and Cullman counties.

co-responder.short: A police program in which a mental health clinician rides with an officer on calls involving a person in crisis. Huntsville's followed a council vote in May 2021.

opioid-settlement-funds.short: Money paid under legal settlements with companies that made and distributed opioids. The state, the counties and the cities each receive a share and decide how to spend it.

detoxification.short: Medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs, the first step of treatment. River Crossing is WellStone's 16-bed detox unit in Huntsville, opened on 24 June 2025.

mountain-lakes.short: The community mental health center for Jackson and Marshall counties, in the ring. It became the ring's first Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic in October 2025.

huntsville-hospital.term: Huntsville Hospital Health System (Huntsville Hospital and Crestwood)
huntsville-hospital.short: The hospital system owned by a public authority of the City of Huntsville. Since 31 March 2026 it has included Crestwood Medical Center as well as Huntsville Hospital.

cullman-regional.short: Cullman County's hospital. It offers outpatient psychiatry and a behavioral health area in its emergency room, has no inpatient psychiatric unit, and publishes the county's needs assessment.

days-to-first-evaluation.term: Days to first evaluation (wait for a first appointment)
days-to-first-evaluation.short: The number of days a new patient waits for an initial assessment. At WellStone it fell from 18 days in January 2025 to under one day in December 2025.

group-homes-and-supervised-housing.short: Places to live with staff support for adults with mental illness. WellStone names supervised housing as a priority, and a court official put the wait for a group home at 100 days or more.

suicide-rate.short: Deaths by suicide per 100,000 residents, averaged over several years. County Health Rankings gives 15.3 for Madison County and 20.7 for Cullman County.

drop-in-center.short: A free, voluntary community space for people with mental illness, outside clinical care. The state lists one in north Alabama, in Huntsville, and none in Cullman County.

prospective-payment.short: The fixed amount Medicaid pays a certified clinic for each day it gives a Medicaid enrollee a qualifying service, whatever the service. It is not paid for people outside Medicaid.

medicaid.short: The public health insurance program for low-income people, paid for jointly by the federal government and the state and run in Alabama by the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

supported-housing.short: Long-term housing paired with support services, aimed at people leaving homelessness. In the Huntsville continuum it went from 334 beds in 2022 to 190 in 2025.

form-990.short: The Internal Revenue Service form on which a nonprofit reports its yearly revenue, expenses and assets. WellStone's latest on the public record is for the year ending September 2021.

uncompensated-care.short: Care a provider delivers and is not paid for. WellStone reports nearly $3.4 million for fiscal year 2025; the Huntsville Hospital system's audit gives about $144.4 million.

intellectual-disability-310-boards.term: Madison County 310 Board and Cullman County 310 Authority
intellectual-disability-310-boards.short: The two local boards that coordinate services for people with intellectual disabilities, one in each county. They are separate from WellStone, the 310 board for mental illness.

appropriation.short: Legal permission to spend a set amount of public money in a given year, granted by a legislature, council or commission. It is made one year at a time.

fiscal-year.short: A budget year, named for the year in which it ends. Alabama's runs from 1 October to 30 September, and WellStone's also ends in September.

strategic-plan.short: The two-year plan WellStone files with the Department of Mental Health. The current one, signed on 18 November 2025, names its service area, people served and unmet needs.

community-health-needs-assessment.short: A periodic local study of a community's health needs. Cullman Regional publishes one for Cullman County; Madison County's nearest equivalent is a 2024 United Way assessment.

be-the-rock.short: WellStone's private fundraising campaign, launched in spring 2021, toward the cost of the crisis center and later the pediatric unit. Its page publishes no goal or total.

aces.term: State evaluation office (Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services)
aces.short: The state commission that evaluates whether state programs work. Its September 2025 report on the crisis centers found their monthly reporting inconsistent.

samhsa.term: SAMHSA (Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration)
samhsa.short: The federal agency for mental health and addiction services, part of the Department of Health and Human Services. It made three grants to WellStone between fiscal years 2021 and 2025.

first-stop.short: A Huntsville nonprofit serving homeless people. It received $810,000 of the city's first opioid settlement allocations and was named as one of the first stops for WellStone's mobile clinic.

crisis-services-of-north-alabama.short: An organization that runs a 24-hour crisis counseling line, a domestic violence shelter and sexual assault services, and manages 2-1-1 for Madison and five nearby counties.

marketplace.term: Health insurance marketplace (and its tax credits)
marketplace.short: The federal exchange where people without job-based coverage buy insurance, often with a subsidy. About 95,000 Alabamians left it after enhanced tax credits expired at the end of 2025.

coverage-gap.short: Adults who earn too much for Alabama's Medicaid and too little for subsidized marketplace insurance. Alabama has not expanded Medicaid, and no county estimate of the gap was found.

medicaid-rehabilitative-services.short: The Medicaid benefit that pays for community mental health treatment. A mental health provider must be a center certified by the Department of Mental Health, which in these two counties is WellStone.

institution-for-mental-disease.term: Institution for mental disease (and Alabama's federal waiver)
institution-for-mental-disease.short: Medicaid's term for a psychiatric facility of more than 16 beds, where it usually will not pay for adults aged 21 to 64. Alabama's waiver covers such stays only in Baldwin and Mobile counties.

all-kids.short: Alabama's Children's Health Insurance Program. With its Medicaid expansion group it covered 12,741 children in Madison County and 4,757 in Cullman County in July 2026.

commercial-insurance.term: Commercial insurance (employer coverage and Blue Cross)
commercial-insurance.short: Private health insurance, most often obtained through a job. Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Alabama held 82% of the Huntsville area's commercial market at the start of 2024.

uninsured-rate.short: The share of people with no health insurance. Two versions appear here: people under 65 (8.3% in Madison, 11.9% in Cullman) and all ages in 2024 (7.72% and 10.9%).

medicaid-eligibles.short: Alabama Medicaid's count of people eligible for the program. A monthly count and the share eligible at any point in a year are different measures and give different percentages.

eight-domains.short: The framework this report shares with the statewide report: eight domains of a mental health system, followed by four sections on systems outside the Department of Mental Health.

inpatient-psychiatric-unit.short: A hospital unit where people are admitted for psychiatric care. Huntsville Hospital describes units for adults and seniors; Cullman County's hospital lists outpatient psychiatry only.

nova-center.short: WellStone's service for children and adolescents in Huntsville, offering individual, group and family counseling. A similar name, NOVA-Huntsville, belongs to its psychosis program.

withdrawal-management.short: Medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs in a staffed unit, often called detox. WellStone's River Crossing unit in Huntsville has 16 beds.

first-episode-psychosis.short: Team-based early treatment for young people having a first psychotic episode. WellStone runs NOVA-Huntsville, one of Alabama's three such programs.

mobile-mental-health-clinic.short: A van WellStone announced in November 2025, to offer therapy and dispense psychiatric medication, starting at First Stop and the Downtown Rescue Mission.

in-state-answer-rate.short: The share of 988 calls from Alabama answered by a counselor in the state instead of rolling over to a national backup center.

helpline.short: A confidential 24-hour crisis counseling telephone line run by Crisis Services of North Alabama, separate from the 988 call center at WellStone.

observation-beds.short: Short-stay beds in a crisis center where a person is watched and treated for hours or a few days without being admitted to a hospital.

state-hospital.short: A psychiatric hospital owned and run by the state. North Alabama's, in Decatur, closed in 2015, which left the state's remaining hospitals in Tuscaloosa.

bryce-hospital.short: The state's psychiatric hospital for adults, in Tuscaloosa. An adult from north Alabama who is committed to a state bed is sent there.

decatur-morgan-west.short: A hospital campus in Decatur, Morgan County, licensed for 64 psychiatric beds and used mainly for children and adolescents. It lies outside Madison and Cullman counties.

unity-psychiatric-care.short: A 20-bed psychiatric hospital in Huntsville giving inpatient care to people aged 55 and older.

state-health-plan.term: State Health Plan (psychiatric bed need rule)
state-health-plan.short: Alabama's planning rule for inpatient psychiatric beds. It decides by region when more beds may be added; Madison and Cullman fall in a ten-county North Region.

crisis-residential.short: A small staffed residence where a person in crisis can stay for a short period as an alternative to a hospital ward.

bradford-health-services.short: A private addiction treatment provider whose campus in the city of Madison offers medical detox, residential treatment and medication-assisted treatment.

medication-assisted-treatment.short: Treating opioid addiction with a prescribed medicine, such as buprenorphine or methadone, usually alongside counseling.

heads-up.short: WellStone's prevention program, which has taught Mental Health First Aid to faculty and staff at the University of Alabama in Huntsville since 2023.

mental-health-first-aid.short: An eight-hour course that teaches members of the public to recognize and respond to someone developing a mental health problem or in crisis.

our-place.short: The one drop-in center for people with mental illness that the Department of Mental Health lists in north Alabama, on Max Luther Drive in Huntsville.

recovery-organization-of-support-special.short: A peer-run organization supporting recovery from substance use. The Department of Mental Health lists Huntsville among its locations and none in Cullman.

peer-living-room.short: A walk-in space where peers offer support. WellStone's 2022 federal grant promised one serving 400 people; no source says whether it opened.

follow-up-after-hospitalization.short: A measure of continuity: the share of people who see a mental health provider soon after leaving a psychiatric hospital. No result for WellStone is published.

time-to-services.short: How long a new patient waits: days to an initial evaluation and days to a first therapy session. It is one of the measures a certified clinic must report.

fox-army-health-center.short: The military clinic on Redstone Arsenal. Its behavioral health department serves service members, families, retirees and civilian employees on weekdays.

va-facilities.short: The federal Department of Veterans Affairs' own sites for veterans. Huntsville has an outpatient clinic and a Vet Center; no VA site is listed in Cullman County.

hpsa.short: A place, population or facility the federal government has designated as short of mental health providers. Cullman County has one; Madison County has no area designation.

low-income-designation.short: A shortage designation for the low-income people of an area: too few providers serve Medicaid and sliding-fee patients for the size of that population.

hpsa-score.short: A number attached to each federal shortage designation. Federal loan repayment for clinicians is tied to the score of the site where they work.

workforce-availability.term: Provider ratio (residents per mental health provider)
workforce-availability.short: The number of residents for each mental health provider of any kind. Published figures for Madison and Cullman differ by source and by who is counted.

kids-count.short: A collection of indicators of child well-being for Alabama and each county, compiled by VOICES for Alabama's Children.

provider-registry.short: The national list of health care providers' identifier numbers, used to count mental health providers by county. It can include people no longer practicing.

psychiatry-residency.short: The years of supervised training a doctor completes after medical school to become a psychiatrist. A four-year program in Huntsville takes up to six residents a year.

psychiatric-mental-health-nurse-practiti.short: An advanced practice nurse specializing in mental health care. The University of Alabama in Huntsville offers a training track requiring 720 clinical hours.

national-health-service-corps.term: Federal loan repayment (National Health Service Corps)
national-health-service-corps.short: A federal program that repays clinicians' student loans in return for at least two years of work at an approved site in a shortage area.

sliding-fee-scale.short: A charge that falls with a patient's income, so that people with low incomes pay little or nothing.

adph.short: The state public health agency, separate from the Department of Mental Health. It keeps the statistics on deaths, including suicides and overdoses.

one-health-record.term: Health information exchange (Alabama One Health Record)
one-health-record.short: Alabama's network for sharing patient records electronically between hospitals, clinics and other providers. Certified clinics must connect their record systems to it.

telehealth.short: Care delivered at a distance by video or telephone.

ccbhc-provider-manual.term: CCBHC provider manual (the state's clinic manual)
ccbhc-provider-manual.short: The Department of Mental Health's rulebook for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics: what they must provide, how they are paid and how they must be run.

community-free-clinic.short: A free clinic in Huntsville for uninsured Madison County residents, with an on-site dispensary where prescriptions are filled. It lists no mental health service.

opioid-treatment-program.short: A clinic certified to dispense methadone, and often buprenorphine, for opioid use disorder. Huntsville has two and Cullman one.

methadone-and-buprenorphine.short: Two medicines prescribed to treat opioid addiction. They reduce craving and withdrawal and lower the risk of overdose.

naloxone.short: A medicine that reverses an opioid overdose within minutes, often given as a nasal spray.

alabama-opioid-overdose-and-addiction-co.term: Alabama Opioid Overdose and Addiction Council
alabama-opioid-overdose-and-addiction-co.short: The state council that reports each year on opioid overdose and addiction in Alabama, including where naloxone has been distributed.

huntsville-transit.term: Huntsville Transit (Orbit buses and Access paratransit)
huntsville-transit.short: The City of Huntsville's public transport: Orbit, the fixed-route bus, and Access, a booked service for riders who cannot use the standard bus.

tram.term: TRAM (Transportation for Rural Areas of Madison County)
tram.short: Madison County's rural public transport outside Huntsville: a weekday service on which a ride must be booked a day ahead.

carts.short: Cullman County's only public transit: a county-run weekday service, 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., on which a ride must be booked by 2:30 p.m. the day before.

demand-response.short: Public transport that runs on booked trips instead of a fixed route: the rider reserves a ride in advance.

community-mental-health-officer.short: A sheriff's deputy appointed by the Madison County probate judge, with more than 80 hours of crisis training, to respond to people in a mental health crisis.

authorized-and-licensed-beds.short: Counts of the beds a hospital is permitted to operate. The hospital association's figures cover a whole hospital and do not show how many of its beds are psychiatric.

certificate-of-need.term: Certificate of need (state approval for hospital beds)
certificate-of-need.short: The state's permission for a hospital to build or add beds. Alabama's review board approved a $150 million tower at Huntsville Hospital in November 2024.

hemsi.short: Madison County's not-for-profit ambulance service, which reports more than 65,000 calls a year. Its home page publishes nothing on behavioral health transports.

ccbhc-quality-measures.short: The results a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic must report: five measures the clinic collects itself and twelve the state calculates.

ccbhc-quality-report.short: An annual report on clinic and state quality measures that the Department of Mental Health's manual says it will produce. None had appeared by 4 October 2026.

drug-overdose-death-rate.short: Deaths from drug overdose for every 100,000 residents. Two sources give different figures for Cullman County, 35.6 and 26.4, for different periods.

poor-mental-health-days.short: A County Health Rankings measure given as a number of days a month: 5.4 in Madison County and 5.7 in Cullman County in the March 2026 figures.

serious-emotional-disturbance.short: The children's counterpart of serious mental illness: a diagnosable disorder in someone under 18 that seriously limits life at home, at school or with others.

census-tract.short: A small area within a county for which statistics are published. The federal PLACES estimates of local health go down to this level.

coroner.short: The county official whose office investigates deaths. Local counts of suicides and overdoses come from coroners and reach the public mainly through news interviews.

ed-boarding.short: Holding a psychiatric patient in an emergency room, sometimes for days, because no inpatient bed or placement is available.

project-zero-suicide.short: A suicide prevention initiative that Cullman Regional Medical Center says it has joined. No results have been reported.

frequent-mental-distress.short: A federal estimate of the share of a county's adults who report frequent mental distress: 18.9% in Cullman County and 16.0% in Madison County in 2023.

disability-waivers.term: Disability waivers (Medicaid waivers for developmental disabilities)
disability-waivers.short: Medicaid waivers for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, run by the Department of Mental Health. The statewide waiting list stood at 1,800 people in May 2025.

area-agency-on-aging.short: A regional body designated by the state to plan and run services for older people. Madison and Cullman counties fall under different ones.

clas-standards.short: A health service's duty to offer interpreters and other language help to people who speak little English. Alabama's clinic manual places it on WellStone.

nami-madison-county.short: The local affiliate of the National Alliance on Mental Illness. It runs peer and family support groups and a course for families. No affiliate is listed for Cullman County.

peer-recovery-center.short: A community center for people seeking recovery from addiction, staffed by peers who are in recovery themselves. The state lists one in Huntsville and none in Cullman County.

lived-experience.short: Personal experience of a mental or substance use disorder, one's own or a family member's. Alabama's clinic manual requires such people to have a part in governing a certified clinic.

the-link-of-cullman-county.short: A Cullman nonprofit that works against poverty. It runs a food pantry, won a 2020 federal grant for a reentry program for people leaving jail or prison, and is an accredited family resource center.

system-of-care.term: System of care (children's mental health framework)
system-of-care.short: A national framework holding that services for children with serious mental health needs should be family-driven, community-based and coordinated across agencies.

school-based-mental-health.term: School-based mental health services (School-Based Mental Health Collaboration)
school-based-mental-health.short: Therapy and other mental health care delivered on school grounds. In Madison County the providers include WellStone and a nonprofit, The Enrichment Center.

dhr.short: Alabama's child welfare agency, responsible for child protection and foster care, with a county office in each of Madison and Cullman counties.

mental-health-services-coordinator.short: A school-district employee who links students and families to mental health services but does not provide treatment. State law requires every district to have one.

brooks-place.short: Cullman County's child advocacy center. It provides forensic interviews, counseling and medical exams at no cost to families and says it is funded entirely by local donations.

forensic-interview.short: An interview, by a specialist at a child advocacy center, of a child who may have been abused or may have witnessed a crime or violent incident.

out-of-home-care.short: The placement of a child, by the child welfare agency, away from the family home: with relatives, with foster parents or in a facility.

indication-of-abuse-or-neglect.term: Children with an indication of abuse or neglect
indication-of-abuse-or-neglect.short: A Kids Count measure: the number of children in a county with an indication of abuse or neglect in a year, also given as a rate per 1,000.

juvenile-alternative-court.term: Alternative Court (Madison County's juvenile specialty courts)
juvenile-alternative-court.short: Madison County's juvenile mental health docket, one of three specialty courts in its juvenile court alongside a drug court and a truancy court.

neaves-davis.short: Madison County's 48-bed juvenile detention center in Huntsville, which holds young people detained by court order.

juvenile-detention.short: Secure custody for young people held by court order while they await a hearing. Madison County's center has 48 beds; Cullman County has a short-term facility of its own.

dys.short: The state's juvenile justice agency. It holds young people committed by juvenile courts and funds local diversion programs, including grants in Madison and Cullman counties.

home-visiting.short: Programs that send a trained visitor to the homes of pregnant women and families with young children to support parenting and health.

infant-and-early-childhood-mental-health.term: Infant and early childhood mental health
infant-and-early-childhood-mental-health.short: Support for the emotional development of children from birth to about five, delivered mainly through the adults who care for them.

paths.term: PATHS (the state's telephone consultation service for pediatricians)
paths.short: A statewide line through which children's doctors can consult child mental health specialists at Children's of Alabama. Families do not call it directly.

sb101-consent-age.short: A 2025 Alabama law raised from 14 to 16 the age below which a student needs a parent's written permission for ongoing school counseling.

sequential-intercept-model.short: A map of the six points, numbered 0 to 5, at which a person with mental illness can be turned from the criminal justice system toward treatment.

office-of-alternative-sentencing-and-rel.term: Office of Alternative Sentencing and Release (Madison County)
office-of-alternative-sentencing-and-rel.short: The Madison County department that runs pretrial release, community corrections, misdemeanor probation, court referral and the adult drug court for the county's courts.

competency-evaluation.short: A defendant's ability to understand the proceedings and help in their own defense. A person found incompetent cannot be tried until competency is restored.

competency-restoration.short: Treatment meant to make a defendant who was found incompetent able to stand trial. It is given at the state forensic hospital or, in seven Alabama counties, inside the jail.

taylor-hardin.term: Taylor Hardin Secure Medical Facility (the state's forensic hospital)
taylor-hardin.short: Alabama's forensic psychiatric hospital, in Tuscaloosa, which treats defendants sent by the criminal courts. In August 2025, 273 men were waiting for a bed.

second-chance-act.short: A federal grant source for programs that help people returning from jail or prison. A $500,000 grant went to The Link of Cullman County in 2020.

reentry.short: The return of a person from prison or jail to the community, and the services that support it. It is Intercept 4 of the Sequential Intercept Model.

pardons-and-paroles.term: Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles (the parole bureau)
pardons-and-paroles.short: The state agency that supervises people on probation and parole. It runs a day reporting center in Huntsville.

day-reporting-center.short: A facility where people on probation or parole who are judged high-risk report for supervision and treatment while living at home. One of Alabama's five is in Huntsville.

community-corrections.short: Locally run programs that supervise people convicted of crimes in the community as an alternative to prison. Madison County's is a public authority; Cullman County's is a nonprofit.

parole-and-probation.short: Probation is supervision in the community in place of prison; parole is supervised release after part of a prison sentence. Both carry conditions and can be revoked.

healthy-people-2030.short: The federal government's set of national health goals for the decade to 2030. This report uses its five-domain grouping of the social conditions that shape health.

north-alabama-coalition-for-the-homeless.term: North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless (the Huntsville continuum)
north-alabama-coalition-for-the-homeless.short: The homelessness continuum of care for Madison, Limestone and Morgan counties. Federal counts and housing inventories for the Huntsville continuum cover all three.

balance-of-state-continuum.short: The homelessness continuum of care that covers 37 Alabama counties, Cullman among them, from Montgomery. It publishes no county-level count.

point-in-time-count.short: A count of everyone found homeless, in shelters and outdoors, on a single night in January. Each homelessness continuum conducts one and the federal housing department publishes it.

housing-inventory-count.short: The federal housing department's yearly list of the beds a homelessness continuum has, by type: emergency shelter, transitional housing, permanent supportive housing and rapid re-housing.

chronic-homelessness.short: A subgroup reported in the federal homelessness count. The Huntsville continuum's January 2025 count listed 128 chronically homeless people.

shelter-plus-care.short: WellStone's permanent supportive housing project, with 24 beds in the 2025 federal housing inventory for the Huntsville continuum.

huntsville-housing-authority.short: The public housing agency for Huntsville, with more than 1,500 rental units and close to 1,800 voucher families. It holds most of the area's permanent supportive housing beds.

housing-choice-voucher.short: Housing assistance, also called Section 8, administered by local housing authorities. Cullman's waiting list is closed; Huntsville's authority assists close to 1,800 families.

coordinated-entry.short: A homelessness continuum's shared entry process for people seeking help. In the Huntsville continuum it is held in person at the Downtown Rescue Mission.

south-derrick-street-camp.short: A camp for unsheltered people in Huntsville that the city manages. It was rebuilt after a 2024 fire with marked spaces and a perimeter fence.

fair-market-rent.short: A benchmark rent for an area. The report cites the hourly wage needed to afford a two-bedroom home at that rent: $25.19 in the Huntsville area and $17.94 in Cullman County.

snap.short: The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, the federal food benefit once called food stamps.

ssi-and-ssdi.short: A federal payment for disabled people with very low income, run by the Social Security Administration. It is separate from the disability insurance earned through past work.

individual-placement-and-support.short: The evidence-based model of supported employment for people with serious mental illness: help finding an ordinary paid job, then lasting support in it.

vocational-rehabilitation.short: The state program that helps people with disabilities prepare for and find work, run by the Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services.

fqhc.term: Federally designated health center (federally qualified health center)
fqhc.short: A federally funded community clinic that provides primary care to anyone, with fees scaled to income. HAPPI Health has four sites, all in Huntsville.

family-resource-center.short: An organization accredited within the Alabama Network of Family Resource Centers. The Link of Cullman County became the state's 28th in September 2026.

mental-health-center-of-north-central-al.term: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama
mental-health-center-of-north-central-al.short: The community mental health center for Lawrence, Limestone and Morgan counties, based in Decatur. One of the four centers that serve the ring.

ced-mental-health-center.short: The community mental health center for Cherokee, DeKalb and Etowah counties in northeast Alabama. One of the four centers that serve the ring.

northwest-alabama-mental-health-center.short: The community mental health center for Fayette, Lamar, Marion, Walker and Winston counties. It runs its own mobile crisis service and crisis residential beds.

census-quickfacts.short: The Census Bureau's summary profile of population, income, insurance and other figures for a county or city. Appendix A takes population, income and uninsured rates from it.

crisis-system.short: The services for a mental health emergency: a line to call, a team that comes, and a place to go that is neither an emergency room nor a jail.

american-community-survey.short: The Census Bureau's continuous household survey. Its five-year estimates are the only survey figures published for areas as small as a census tract.

margin-of-error.short: The range around a survey estimate within which the true value probably lies. For a small area such as a census tract it is often wide.

cdc-places.short: A federal dataset of modeled health estimates for counties, cities and census tracts. Its tract values are produced by a model, not by surveying each tract.

open-items.short: The list of things this report could not read, confirm or find, each with where it was looked for and what would settle it.

claims-ledger.short: The record behind the report: every claim it makes, the passage that supports it, and whether it is verified, the report's own analysis, or a statement that something was not found.
